resources.title: Roux Beginner Supplemental Guide (linked as "Noblion's Beginner Reference Sheet")
resources.author: Noblion (per the rouxcubing.com link text; the doc itself names no author)
resources.level: beginner (first-time Roux solvers; supplements a text tutorial)
resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc. It is a picture-plus-moves reference for a complete beginner Roux solve in 3 numbered parts, with 34 embedded images. Most images are 3D isometric renders in which unsolved or irrelevant pieces are ghosted, so only the pieces that matter show in colour. (1) 'Solve the left and right blocks' has two 2-column tables (case image | move sequence). Left Block has 6 piece-insertion cases: placing the DL edge and inserting the front and back pairs. Right Block has 10 cases: inserting the DR edge, then pairs in various orientations. Each case has one short intuitive sequence of 1 to 3 moves. (2) 'Solve the Corners' is a 2-alg beginner corner method. Sune is repeated for orientation, with a written setup rule (set up so exactly one yellow corner faces up, put it front-left, repeat Sune). One corner-swap alg (J-perm) does permutation, recognised by 'two matching colours on the same side' (headlights), or applied once when there are none. (3) LSE: the edge-orientation step defines good and bad edges against the U/D colours and uses a 3-move flip sequence plus two 'Front Swap' and 'Back Swap' M2-style swaps to reach a 3-top/1-bottom bad-edge state. It then resolves that state with an 'arrow' rule: point the top arrow at the bottom bad edge, then do U and M once each. Next, UL/UR: move the two yellow side-colour edges to the bottom with the swaps, set U so the front stickers are opposite the bottom centre (2 options), then M2 and U/U'. Last, the M-slice: a 6-case table (pure M/U2 sequences) plus a written method for the remaining 3-cycle cases (find the isolated edge, put it on top, U2, repeat). Saved: plain-text export, HTML export and the extracted images (beginner-ref-imgs/).

resources.title: Frameworks: a structured approach to blocks (tab: 'First Block (Frameworks)')
resources.author: Shadowslice (per the rouxcubing.com and resources.rouxers.com link text)
resources.level: intermediate to advanced (inspection and FB planning; SB approach choice)
resources.summary: A short single-tab prose guide (about 1,100 words, no images, no algs) on planning First Block in inspection through 'frameworks'. A framework is an intermediate cubestate 1-4 moves from solved FB that you know well enough to finish automatically. You plan only 3-4 moves to the framework instead of 6-10 to a full FB, and you scan the scramble for features that suggest which 'type of block' to aim for. Line-line and square-pair are named as the simplest 1-move frameworks. Concrete training prescription: learn all 3-move and some 4-move FB cases with onionhoney's Block Trainer (linked to onionhoney.github.io/roux-trainers/#fb). Minimum benchmarks are 90% success at depth 3 and 50% at depth 4, with solutions found 'near-instantly'. Then stop grinding and move to real solves, because pattern recognition only develops on real scrambles. Scramble features that push you towards a framework: free pairs, mismatched pairs, corner-edge configurations. Practice method: high volume; start with unlimited inspection; try several frameworks per scramble; learn when to abandon one quickly; treat trainer work and real solves as a feedback loop. Addenda: zwischenzugs (in-between moves that influence other pieces without disrupting the solution, likened to FMC), used to carry FB's last moves into SB; tracing how each framework moves SB pieces, for lookahead; three SB 'frameworks' (pair-first/classical: most efficient but harder lookahead; DR-first: easiest lookahead and least efficient, the common beginner approach; DR-neutral: one SB edge plus its pair, pairs possibly out of order with F R' F'-type moves), and choosing among them by cubestate; why top solvers say they 'don't plan FB' (they plan to a framework subconsciously); and why planning FBSS directly is not recommended (most good FBSS solutions are FB then SS anyway). Saved: text and HTML export.

resources.title: Recognising blocks via its "L/R" stickers (linked as "SB Pair Inspection" / "Neo's insight on recognizing blocks")
resources.author: Fahmi and Neo (per rouxcubing.com); 'Neo' (per resources.rouxers.com). The hidden 'SB Theory' tab credits Rodney Kinney's HTR Theory as its basis.
resources.level: intermediate (recognition concept); the hidden SB Theory tab is aimed at beginners
resources.summary: A Google Sheet with 1 visible tab ('Recognition', gid 146348617) and 2 hidden tabs ('List' and 'SB Theory'). The hidden tabs come through the public xlsx export; htmlview lists only the visible tab. 'Recognition' argues in 5 rows of prose that SB pairs should be recognised by the colours of the square they will form, the pair's 'L/R' (side) stickers, rather than as CFOP F2L pairs. Reasons given: short blockbuilding solutions become intelligible; solutions that form different pieces but the same squares are grouped together; and a pair after a square can be recognised from just 2 stickers. Two worked examples, one FB and one SB. The cost: it gives up attributes such as EO, which 'more efficient solutions have shown' are not useful here. Each example is drawn with visualcube IMAGE() formulas that use sticker masks: only the relevant stickers are coloured and the rest transparent, some with arrows. It links to Shadowslice's Frameworks doc ('Discussed here'). Hidden 'List' holds 64 SB pair cases, each with a right-slot solution and its mirrored left-slot version. Trailing M-slice restores are in parentheses. The list is imported by IMPORTRANGE from a private sheet (401 when fetched). It has instructions for drilling them in namisama269's 3BLD-Alg-Trainer by pasting the algs and an 'Initial Mask' string that hides all stickers except the relevant ones, 'because Zhouheng's [onionhoney's] trainers can't partially cover such stickers, yet'. A screenshot shows a masked cube. Hidden 'SB Theory' is a beginner system: a table of corner location (in U, in RDF, in RDB) by destination (RDF, RDB), giving generic move families ('any R* U* R* sequence that twists the corner and keeps it on U', continue arrows), so a learner can solve an SB pair from 2 corner attributes before learning algs. Saved: CSV of the visible tab, a text dump of all 3 tabs (values, links, IMPORTRANGE note), the xlsx and the embedded screenshot.

resources.title: Second Block Algs (linked as "Kian's Second Block Last Pair Algs and Louis' other tricks")
resources.author: Kian and Louis (per resources.rouxers.com link text; section heading names Louis). Commonly attributed to Kian Mansour and Louis de Mendonça, but the doc does not say so
resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc of SB alg tables with 63 embedded 2D isometric case diagrams. Only the F2B and relevant SB pieces are coloured: red/green/white for the FR pair, the rest dark. Section 1, 'Front Pair Cases with DR Solved', covers the last SB pair (FR corner + edge) with the DR edge and back (BR) square already solved. It has 7 two-column tables of image + alg cells: 47 real cases, plus 1 joke cell that shows the solved state with filler text ('Pizza would be Proud', 'LOLOLOL...'). Each case lists 1 to 7 alternative algs, mostly R/r/U/M with some F and D. Many alternatives are marked '(free slot)', meaning they need the BR slot free or use D moves. Cases are grouped implicitly, without headings, by where the FR corner is and how it is twisted (in U facing front, right or up; in the DFR slot), with the edge position varying inside each group. A final group covers edge-in-slot and both-in-slot situations. No case names, numbers or recognition text. Section 2, 'Louis' Multislotting and F-Move Happy Place', has 15 image + alg cells (1 to 3 algs each) of F/f/S/B-move tricks: pair inserts that also fix or keep other SB pieces, a pair-swap image, and insertions when DR or the other pair is not yet solved. Saved: text and HTML export plus all 63 images (sb-algs-imgs/).

resources.title: RUroux/CPRoux Spreadsheet (linked as "Edde's CP Roux Sheet")
resources.author: Edde (per the rouxcubing.com link text; the sheet links to edde.github.io tools). It credits Trangium for the cp-nautilus FR-in-DF idea
resources.level: advanced / experimental (a CP-first Roux variant; the sheet itself says most FR-in-DF algs are untested)
resources.summary: A Google Sheet with 10 visible tabs and 1 hidden tab: Main, CMLL, WV, SV, FR in DF, TCMLL, DR flipped, FR flipped, (S)L5C, Sune, and hidden 'Last pair setup', which is empty apart from 'WIP'. It collects algs and tricks for CP-first Roux, also called RUroux: 2-gen reduction during FB. Steps: CPFB (influence DR), SS (influence OCLS, done in dRf or dRb), OCLS (orient corners and finish the last slot, influence EO), LSE (EOLR or L7E). It is explicitly not a general Roux guide and does not cover LSE or SS. Its OH focus: 'it's unclear if L7E is particularly good for OH', so it recommends CMLL/WV/TCMLL before L5C. The Main tab explains the method, defines L5C and SL5C (Short Last 5 Corners: algs that need only U* R' to finish, set up for an edge insert), and describes Trangium's FR-in-DF idea (FR edge parked in DF, solved with r U' R' alongside L5C; about 1 move more than plain SS). It notes that R and r are often interchangeable for edge influence (marked by underlining) and that algs were generated with Batch Solver in RUr-gen. It links CPFB resources: UCPT doc, YruRU CP tracing, Circlets, CEOR-Zero, 2-gen FB doc, a 0-move CPFB sheet and edde.github.io/FBtrainer. It also links 2 Discord servers (the 0-move server, preferred for RUroux, and the CEOR server) and has a to-do list (more ACMLL, BLS, conjugation, 'tyrannical caterpillar' for L5C). Every alg tab follows one structure: a case image from a visualcube IMAGE() formula built from the first alg (inverse case), with a sticker mask and a 'Plane view'/'3D view' toggle. Up to 6 alternatives per case each carry auto-computed STM and SQTM counts, and some tabs show a per-group or per-set average STM. Cases have no names; they are grouped by subset headings. Saved: CSV of all 10 visible tabs, the xlsx (including the hidden tab), a text dump of every tab with links, and the Main-tab illustration.
